content.text:
### Turn a list into a causal account
Start with the Crown's fiscal predicament. Explain why attempts to resolve it required political negotiation, then examine how disputes over representation changed the crisis. Add popular pressures without assuming that one strand determines the whole story. Distinguish evidence for each link from hindsight about the eventual outcome.

References: [Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis: fiscal history research](https://www.minneapolisfed.org/article/1991/the-macroeconomic-causes-and-consequences-of-the-french-revolution), [The National Archives: contemporary reports](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/education/teaching-resources/french-revolution/).

### The monarchy's fiscal crisis
The French monarchy faced a serious fiscal crisis before the Estates-General met in 1789.

### A political response in 1789
Louis XVI convened the Estates-General in 1789 in the context of the monarchy's fiscal and political crisis.

### From finance to representation
Attempts to address the French monarchy's fiscal crisis brought disputes over taxation and political representation into the Estates-General.

messages.content: Since we know the monarchy eventually fell, can we write as if everyone in 1789 knew that would happen?

content.text:
Later knowledge belongs to the historian, not automatically to the actors. Reconstruct what people could know and what options they perceived at the time. A causal explanation can identify pressures without claiming an inevitable destination.

### Material and political pressures
Food insecurity and economic distress formed part of the context of popular mobilisation in revolutionary France.

### An explanation with several causes
A historical explanation of 1789 can connect fiscal crisis, institutional conflict, and popular pressures rather than treating one factor as sufficient.

### Outcomes were contingent
Explaining pressures before the French Revolution does not establish that each later revolutionary outcome was inevitable.
